$comment: Pinned downloads for the embedded Python runtime that ships inside Project CHAOS.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  The installed product must not require Python to be
preinstalled, so the build pulls the official Windows embeddable CPython
distribution and turns it into a self-contained python\ tree.  A control
system that silently downloads and executes an unverified interpreter is not
acceptable: the interpreter it runs is the thing that decides whether a pump
starts.  Every artefact below is pinned by SHA-256 and python-runtime.ps1
refuses to continue on a mismatch.  There is no --skip-hash switch.
HOW THESE DIGESTS WERE OBTAINED (2026-08-07, recorded so they can be redone):
1. curl the artefact and its detached .asc signature from www.python.org/ftp
2. gpg --verify <artefact>.asc <artefact>
-> Good signature from 'Steve Dower (Python Release Signing)'
primary key fingerprint 7ED1 0B65 31D7 C8E1 BC29  6021 FC62 4643 4870 34E5
(the CPython Windows release-manager key)
3. sha256sum <artefact>  -> the value recorded here
So the digest is not trust-on-first-use: it is derived from bytes that carry a
good signature from the CPython Windows release manager.  Anyone changing a pin
is expected to repeat steps 1-3 and update the provenance block, not to paste a
digest from a build log.
The pip wheel digest is the sha256 published by PyPI for that exact file
(https://pypi.org/pypi/pip/26.2.1/json), which is what pip itself checks.

provenance.method: detached OpenPGP signature verified, then SHA-256 taken of the verified bytes

notes: This is the version the platform is developed and tested against:
pyproject requires-python >= 3.11, ruff target-version py311, and the
Python CI matrix is ['3.11'].  A control system ships the configuration
that was tested, not the newest one.
KNOWN LIMITATION, READ BEFORE A LONG DEPLOYMENT: 3.11.9 is the LAST
CPython 3.11 release with Windows binaries.  3.11.10 and later are
source-only security releases, so this embeddable will never receive a
python.org security update.  Moving up is a one-line change here plus a
matching entry in the Python CI matrix; see docs/windows-deployment.md
section 'Embedded Python runtime'.
Last CPython 3.12 release with Windows binaries.  Not yet exercised by
the Python test suite; add '3.12' to the CI matrix in
.github/workflows/ci.yml before shipping it.
Current maintained line with Windows binaries.  This is where the
runtime should end up once the platform test suite runs green on 3.13.
Not yet exercised by the Python test suite.
The embeddable distribution ships no pip and no ensurepip, so pip is
bootstrapped by putting this wheel on sys.path and running the pip module
out of it (a wheel is a zip and zipimport can load from it):
python.exe <wheel>\pip install --no-index <wheel>
That keeps the bootstrap a single hash-pinned file instead of a get-pip.py
whose contents change without notice.
